title: Inspection of the Passenger Oxygen Chemical Generators and the Distribution Manifold
abstract: Scheduled inspection of the passenger oxygen chemical generators, their lanyards and the distribution manifold, with the sample drop test that confirms the release mechanism across a cabin zone.

sections.purpose: This task inspects the chemical oxygen generators in the passenger service units, checks the lanyard routing and the generator life, and confirms the release mechanism by a sample drop test.
sections.job_setup_note: A chemical oxygen generator that has been fired is very hot and stays hot for a long time. Never handle a fired generator without the gloves specified in the instructions. Do not pull a lanyard during the inspection; the drop test is done from the flight deck control so that the generators are not fired. Have the transport container ready before any unit is opened.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the passenger oxygen system is safetied at the flight deck control. WARNING: NEVER HANDLE A FIRED CHEMICAL OXYGEN GENERATOR WITHOUT THE SPECIFIED GLOVES. A FIRED GENERATOR REACHES 250 DEGREES AND STAYS HOT FOR MORE THAN AN HOUR. 2. Get access to the passenger service units through the ceiling panels in zones 254 and 265. 3. Open each unit in the sample group given in the instructions. 4. Record the life expiry date of each generator. CAUTION: DO NOT PULL A LANYARD WHILE THE UNIT IS OPEN. A PULLED LANYARD FIRES THE GENERATOR AND THE UNIT CANNOT BE RECOVERED. 5. Check that each lanyard is routed clear of the mask hose and that no lanyard is trapped by the unit door. 6. Check the percussion cap for corrosion and for security. 7. Check the thermal blanket in the unit cavity for displacement and for heat marking. 8. Close each unit and confirm that the door latches. 9. Do a pressure and leak check of the distribution manifold at the accumulator D3520114349032 and at the filter D3520117593776, and record the decay over the period given in the instructions. 10. Do the sample drop test from the flight deck control on the units listed in the instructions and confirm that every door in the sample releases. 11. Reset the released doors, confirm that they latch, and compare the manifold arrangement with drawings D35201154822 and D35201170600.
sections.close_out: Restore the ceiling panels and confirm the tool count. Restore the flight deck control to the normal position and remove the safety. Record the generator life expiry dates, the manifold decay figure and the drop test result on the maintenance record.

safety_precautions: Safety the passenger oxygen system at the flight deck control.
Never handle a fired generator without the specified gloves.
Do not pull a lanyard during the inspection.

title: Inspection of the Passenger Oxygen Chemical Generators and the Distribution Manifold

issue.reason: A duration marking check is added at each opened unit and the sample size is qualified as valid only for a cabin of one generator duration.

abstract: Scheduled inspection of the passenger oxygen chemical generators, their lanyards and the distribution manifold, including the sample drop test that confirms the release mechanism across a cabin zone.

sections.purpose: This task inspects the chemical oxygen generators in the passenger service units, checks the lanyard routing and the generator life, and confirms the release mechanism by a sample drop test. The sample size is derived from a cabin in which every generator is of the same duration; it has no statistical meaning across a cabin carrying two durations, which is why the duration marking is read at every unit that is opened.
sections.job_setup_note: A chemical oxygen generator that has been fired is very hot and stays hot for a long time. Never handle a fired generator without the gloves specified in the instructions. Do not pull a lanyard during the inspection; the drop test is done from the flight deck control so that the generators are not fired. Mixed generator durations in one cabin are not permitted, so record the duration marking of every unit you open. If two durations are found the sample is void: report the aircraft and do not close the task on the sample result.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the passenger oxygen system is safetied at the flight deck control. WARNING: NEVER HANDLE A FIRED CHEMICAL OXYGEN GENERATOR WITHOUT THE SPECIFIED GLOVES. A FIRED GENERATOR REACHES 250 DEGREES AND STAYS HOT FOR MORE THAN AN HOUR. 2. Get access to the passenger service units through the ceiling panels in zones 254 and 265. 3. Open each unit in the sample group given in the instructions. 4. Record the generator duration marking and the life expiry date of each generator. CAUTION: DO NOT MIX GENERATOR DURATIONS IN ONE CABIN. IF A UNIT OF A DIFFERENT DURATION IS FOUND, STOP AND REPORT IT BEFORE YOU CONTINUE. 5. Check that each lanyard is routed clear of the mask hose and that no lanyard is trapped by the unit door. 6. Check the percussion cap for corrosion and for security. 7. Check the thermal blanket in the unit cavity for displacement and for heat marking. 8. Close each unit and confirm that the door latches. 9. Do a pressure and leak check of the distribution manifold at the accumulator D3520114349032 and at the filter D3520117593776, and record the decay over the period given in the instructions. 10. Do the sample drop test from the flight deck control on the units listed in the instructions and confirm that every door in the sample releases. 11. Reset the released doors and confirm that they latch. 12. Compare the manifold arrangement with drawings D35201154822 and D35201170600 and report any difference.
sections.close_out: Restore the ceiling panels and confirm the tool count. Restore the flight deck control to the normal position and remove the safety. Record the generator life expiry dates, the manifold decay figure and the drop test result on the maintenance record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The duration marking check applies to both the fifteen and the twenty-two minute standard.

Never handle a fired generator without the specified gloves.
Do not pull a lanyard during the inspection.
